source_type_decision.reason: The two source rows carry the same question_id and semantically identical wording, so the mixed taxonomy does not justify splitting the Canonical. The scenario contract is the stricter useful contract here: it directly answers the mechanism question while also requiring failure windows, persistence/idempotency boundaries, recovery and validation.

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.3.1 KafkaProducer API
verified_claims: idempotent producer retries do not introduce duplicate Kafka log records within the documented producer/session boundary, while application-level re-sends cannot be de-duplicated
transactional.id enables the transactional APIs and idempotence
sendOffsetsToTransaction makes consumer offsets part of the current transaction and those offsets are committed only if the transaction commits successfully
transactional end-to-end guarantees require consumers to read only committed messages

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.3 Producer Configs
verified_claims: enable.idempotence defaults to true when there are no conflicting configs
idempotence requires acks=all, retries greater than zero and max.in.flight.requests.per.connection less than or equal to five

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.3 Consumer Configs
verified_claims: read_committed returns committed transactional messages and is bounded by the last stable offset while transactions remain open

primary_sources_checked.title: MySQL 8.4 Introduction to InnoDB
verified_claims: InnoDB DML follows the ACID model with commit, rollback and crash recovery

primary_sources_checked.title: MySQL 8.4 PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE Index Constraints
verified_claims: duplicate unique-key changes produce constraint violations and InnoDB rolls back the violating statement

primary_sources_checked.title: MySQL 8.4 INFORMATION_SCHEMA COLUMNS
verified_claims: a UNIQUE index permits multiple NULL values, so a correctness-critical deduplication key must separately enforce non-null key columns

primary_sources_checked.title: Debezium Outbox Event Router
verified_claims: the default outbox event id is NOT NULL and is the unique event ID that can be used for duplicate removal
aggregate id is emitted as the event key and supports partition ordering

findings.message: The answer makes processed_event UNIQUE the correctness boundary for concurrent duplicate delivery, but its schema shorthand never requires consumer/event_id to be NOT NULL. MySQL 8.4 explicitly permits multiple NULL values in a UNIQUE index, so application-level schema validation alone leaves the database invariant under-specified. Define a non-null stable dedup key (preferably an explicit composite PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE over NOT NULL consumer scope + event_id) and keep the event-id scope statement aligned with that constraint.

next_required_action: Revise only the recorded dedup-key nullability/invariant finding, refresh the candidate SHA and review packet, then perform a fresh isolated source-first re-review before evidence binding/audit or any pilot human approval.
